title: Repeated Python authoring friction and malformed bundles consumed valid provider Turns as faults

evidence.locator: candidate_rejected source diagnostics, author_actions_resolved refusals and provider_fault records for over-budget or missing-import Python bundles

observation: The inspected snapshot has 53 explicit across_loop=True refusals, 19 reduction-axis refusals, 17 unauthorized-parent transform calls and 11 result-identity refusals. Valid native CLI Turns with malformed source bundles ended the Run as provider_fault rather than giving the author a no-build refusal to repair.
proposed_change: Canonicalize the explicit Python reduction default and valid negative axes without changing canonical IR admission. Project actual prior Run-local parent identities, exact stage names and fresh output-name suggestions into the author StateCard. Reject an invalid whole source bundle without truncation or compilation, retain raw source and native usage, and allow a later bounded Turn to repair it. Preserve foreign-parent and transformation-grant refusals.

verified_by.CPU_contracts: 214 focused tests passed, including actual invalid-then-repaired independent Run and semantic replay, positive/negative default-axis tests and foreign-parent refusal
verified_by.independent_Compiler_review: Frontend normalization reviewed at fdfee88f, including explicit out=, bool/float/axis boundaries; no blocker
verified_by.scope: Software protocol repair, not provider/hardware optimization qualification

promotion_disposition: Promote after successor integration gates. Old frozen Runs remain classified by their own source; future author errors receive explicit repair feedback and consume their Turn. No numerical, device, model, material or budget relaxation.
